samples.scenario: Attacker sets up a rogue Wi-Fi hotspot in a coffee shop, intercepting user traffic to a banking website.
samples.technical_data: User attempts to access https://bank.com but is redirected to http://bank.com via the attacker's MITM proxy that strips SSL encryption.
samples.indicators: User notices the browser shows 'http' instead of 'https'; absence of padlock icon; unusual certificate warnings are suppressed by attacker.

samples.scenario: Attacker on a public Wi-Fi network intercepts login credentials for an email account by downgrading the connection from HTTPS to HTTP.
samples.technical_data: Using a tool like sslstrip, attacker intercepts DNS requests and rewrites links from https://mail.com to http://mail.com, capturing plaintext credentials.
samples.indicators: User's browser URL bar lacks HTTPS indication; login credentials transmitted in plaintext over the network.

samples.scenario: An attacker performs MITM attack in a corporate LAN, redirecting employees' requests to a secure intranet portal to an insecure version.
samples.technical_data: Attacker modifies HTTP headers and strips SSL from intranet portal URLs, forcing employees to transmit sensitive data unencrypted.
samples.indicators: Network monitoring shows unencrypted traffic where HTTPS is expected; employees report missing security indicators in browser.

samples.scenario: During a conference, an attacker uses ARP spoofing to intercept traffic and downgrade HTTPS connections for a popular social media site.
samples.technical_data: Attacker performs ARP poisoning and runs sslstrip to transparently downgrade https://socialmedia.com to http://socialmedia.com, capturing session cookies.
samples.indicators: Session cookies appear in network logs unencrypted; users report unusual login prompts; browser security warnings are absent due to attacker's suppression.

samples.scenario: Attacker compromises a hotel network router, redirecting guests' secure shopping website connections to unsecure HTTP versions.
samples.technical_data: Modified router firmware redirects https://shopping.com to http://shopping.com; attacker captures credit card information in plaintext via MITM proxy.
samples.indicators: Users notice lack of HTTPS padlock on checkout pages; network scanning reveals HTTP traffic on typically secure domains.
